moves.title: How the pieces move
moves.board.title: The board
moves.board.intro: The board has 64 squares: eight files, from a to h, and eight ranks, from 1 to 8. Every square has a name, like d4: file d, rank 4. White starts at the bottom.
moves.board.ex1: The king moves one square in any direction. From d1, go to d2, then e3, then f4.
moves.board.ex2: Take the rook to h4, then d4, then d1: look at the letters of the files and the numbers of the ranks.
moves.board.ex3: The knight starts on c1. Reach e2, then g3, then f5.
moves.board.ex4: Challenge: the queen starts on e1 and has to touch a5, a8, h8 and h1, the corners and edges of the board.
pieces.rook.title: The rook
pieces.rook.intro: The rook runs straight, along ranks and files, as many squares as you like. It can't jump over other pieces.
pieces.rook.ex1: The rook moves along ranks and files. Collect all the stars.
pieces.rook.ex2: Collect the stars in as few moves as possible.
pieces.rook.ex3: Five stars: choose carefully which one to start with.
pieces.rook.ex4: Challenge: the stars aren't in a line. Think before you move.
pieces.bishop.title: The bishop
pieces.bishop.intro: The bishop runs along diagonals. One bishop starts on a light square and the other on a dark one, and each always stays on its own color.
pieces.bishop.ex1: The bishop moves along diagonals and always stays on the same color. Collect the stars.
pieces.bishop.ex2: Collect the stars in as few moves as possible.
pieces.bishop.ex3: The long diagonals cross the whole board. Collect the stars.
pieces.bishop.ex4: Challenge: five scattered stars, all on the bishop's color.
pieces.queen.title: The queen
pieces.queen.intro: The queen is the strongest piece: she moves like a rook and a bishop combined, in all eight directions.
pieces.queen.ex1: The queen combines rook and bishop. Collect the stars.
pieces.queen.ex2: Collect the stars in as few moves as possible.
pieces.queen.ex3: The queen can stop on an empty square and then change direction.
pieces.queen.ex4: Challenge: five stars scattered all over the board.
pieces.king.title: The king
pieces.king.intro: The king is the most important piece but also the slowest: he takes just one step, in any direction.
pieces.king.ex1: The king moves one square in any direction.
pieces.king.ex2: Collect the stars in as few steps as possible.
pieces.king.ex3: A diagonal step is a shortcut. Collect the stars.
pieces.king.ex4: Challenge: a long trip for the king, in as few steps as possible.
pieces.knight.title: The knight
pieces.knight.intro: The knight jumps in an L shape: two squares straight and one to the side. It's the only piece that can jump over the others.
pieces.knight.ex1: The knight jumps in an L shape and leaps over pieces.
pieces.knight.ex2: Collect the stars in as few moves as possible.
pieces.knight.ex3: Jump from star to star all the way to the other side.
pieces.knight.ex4: Challenge: after each star the knight has to come back. Find the shortest route.
pieces.pawn.title: The pawn
pieces.pawn.intro: The pawn only goes forward, one square at a time. On its first move it can go two. When it reaches the far end it becomes a new piece.
pieces.pawn.ex1: The pawn advances one square, or two on its first move. At the far end it becomes a queen.
pieces.pawn.ex2: Promote the pawn and collect the last star with the new queen.
pieces.pawn.ex3: Promote the pawn, then use the queen for the other stars.
pieces.pawn.ex4: Challenge: collect the stars with the pawn and then with the queen.
moves.pawn-capture.title: The pawn captures sideways
moves.pawn-capture.intro: The pawn advances straight, but captures diagonally, forward. If a piece is right in front of it, it can neither advance nor capture it.
moves.pawn-capture.ex1: Capture the black pawn with your pawn.
moves.pawn-capture.ex2: The e4 pawn is blocked by the black one. Capture with the other pawn, diagonally.
moves.pawn-capture.ex3: The pawn can capture two pieces. Choose the more valuable one.
moves.pawn-capture.ex4: Challenge: capture the rook and reach the far end. The pawn becomes a queen.
moves.which-piece.title: Which piece?
moves.which-piece.intro: Each piece can only go where it knows how to move. Before you move, ask yourself which of your pieces can reach the square you need.
moves.which-piece.ex1: Capture the black pawn on e5: only one white piece can get there.
moves.which-piece.ex2: Give check to the black king with the rook.
moves.which-piece.ex3: Capture the f7 pawn: only the bishop can get there, diagonally.
moves.which-piece.ex4: Challenge: the black queen is hanging. Which white piece can capture her?
pieces.title: Capturing and defending
pieces.capture.title: Capturing
pieces.capture.intro: To capture an enemy piece, move to its square: the captured piece leaves the board. Pieces are not all worth the same: pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9.
pieces.capture.ex1: Capture the knight with the rook.
pieces.capture.ex2: The pawn captures diagonally, forward. Take the bishop.
pieces.capture.ex3: The knight can capture three pieces. Choose the most valuable one.
pieces.capture.ex4: Capture the piece nobody defends, so you don't lose your rook.
pieces.hanging.title: The hanging piece
pieces.hanging.intro: A piece is hanging if an opponent can capture it and nobody defends it. Before you move, look at which pieces, yours and theirs, are undefended.
pieces.hanging.ex1: Capture the black knight: nobody defends it.
pieces.hanging.ex2: Two black pieces: the knight is defended by the pawn, the bishop isn't. Take the one that's hanging.
pieces.hanging.ex3: Your queen is attacked by the bishop, but the bishop is hanging: capture first.
pieces.hanging.ex4: Challenge: before capturing, check whether the piece is defended. Here the black rook is alone.
pieces.defend.title: Defending a piece
pieces.defend.intro: Defending a piece means having another piece that can recapture if it gets taken. A defended piece is safe from trades that don't pay off for the opponent.
pieces.defend.ex1: Your knight is attacked by the black bishop. Defend it with the rook.
pieces.defend.ex2: The e4 pawn is attacked by the bishop. Defend it with the king.
pieces.defend.ex3: The black knight attacks your bishop. Defend it with a pawn.
pieces.defend.ex4: Challenge: the black knight attacks your rook. Defend it with the queen or the king.
rules.title: The rules
rules.check.title: Check
rules.check.intro: When a piece attacks the king, the king is in check. The player in check must save the king right away: no other move is allowed.
rules.check.ex1: Give check to the black king with the rook.
rules.check.ex3: Give check with the bishop: there are two ways.
rules.check.ex4: Give check with the queen, but on a square where the king can't capture her.
rules.escape.title: Escaping check
rules.escape.intro: There are three ways out of check: move the king, capture the piece giving check, or put a piece in between.
rules.escape.ex1: The black rook gives check. Capture the piece that gives check.
rules.escape.ex2: Block the check by putting the knight in between.
rules.escape.ex3: Move the king off the rook's rank, without ending up next to the black king.
rules.escape.ex4: The king is in danger. Find the only move that saves him.
rules.castle.title: How to castle
rules.castle.intro: When you castle, the king takes two steps toward a rook and the rook jumps over him. You can do it if the king and that rook have never moved, there are no pieces between them, and the king doesn't pass through attacked squares.
rules.castle.ex1: Castle kingside, toward the nearer rook.
rules.castle.ex2: Now castle queenside, toward the farther rook.
rules.castle.ex3: The black bishop controls a square the king would pass through. Castle on the right side.
rules.castle.ex4: The knight is between the king and the rook. Move it, then castle kingside.
rules.en-passant.title: En passant
rules.en-passant.intro: If an enemy pawn advances two squares and stops next to yours, on your very next move you can capture it as if it had taken only one step. That's the en passant capture.
rules.en-passant.ex1: The black pawn has just gone from d7 to d5. Capture it en passant.
rules.en-passant.ex2: The black pawn has just gone from c7 to c5. Capture it en passant.
rules.en-passant.ex3: The black pawn has just gone from f7 to f5. Two of your pawns can capture it en passant: use one of them.
rules.en-passant.ex4: The black pawn has just gone from g7 to g5. Capture it en passant: the other black pawn had been there before.
rules.promotion.title: Promotion
rules.promotion.intro: A pawn that reaches the far end turns into a queen, rook, bishop or knight: the queen is almost always the best choice. Here it becomes a queen automatically.
rules.promotion.ex1: Push the pawn all the way to the end: it becomes a queen.
rules.promotion.ex2: Promote the pawn by capturing the rook.
rules.promotion.ex3: Promote the pawn and give checkmate.
rules.promotion.ex4: The black king is far away. Promote the pawn in two moves.
rules.stalemate.title: Stalemate
rules.stalemate.intro: If the player to move isn't in check but has no legal move, the game ends in a draw: that's stalemate. When you're ahead, always leave the enemy king a move until you deliver checkmate.
rules.stalemate.ex1: Deliver checkmate. Careful: one move looks good but it's stalemate.
rules.stalemate.ex2: Deliver checkmate with the queen, without trapping the king in stalemate.
rules.stalemate.ex3: Checkmate in one move. With the rook. Be careful not to leave the black king without moves.
rules.stalemate.ex4: Checkmate in one move. The black king has no moves: if you don't give check, it's stalemate.
mates.title: Basic checkmates
mates.one.title: Mate in one
mates.one.intro: Checkmate means the king is in check and has no way to escape. Checkmate wins the game.
mates.one.ex1: Checkmate in one move. The king is boxed in by his own pawns.
mates.one.ex2: Checkmate in one move. The rooks work like a ladder.
mates.one.ex3: Checkmate in one move. The black king is smothered by his own pieces.
mates.one.ex4: Checkmate in one move. The queen attacks together with the bishop.
mates.back-rank.title: The back-rank mate
mates.back-rank.intro: When the king sits on the back rank boxed in by his own pawns, a rook or queen on that rank delivers checkmate. That's why it's wise to give your king an escape square.
mates.back-rank.ex1: Checkmate in one move. Use the queen.
mates.back-rank.ex2: Checkmate in one move. The black knight defends a square on the back rank: choose the right rook.
mates.back-rank.ex3: Checkmate in two moves. The black rook defends the back rank: lure it away.
mates.back-rank.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. Your rooks are doubled: they're stronger than the black ones.
mates.queen.title: Queen and king
mates.queen.intro: The queen alone isn't enough for checkmate: she needs the king's help, either protecting her or taking away the enemy king's escape squares.
mates.queen.ex1: Checkmate in one move. Your king helps you.
mates.queen.ex2: Checkmate in one move. The black king is on the edge.
mates.queen.ex3: Checkmate in one move. The queen works together with the king.
mates.queen.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. First bring the king closer, then the queen delivers mate.
mates.rooks.title: The rook ladder
mates.rooks.intro: Two rooks can deliver checkmate on their own: one cuts off a rank, the other gives check on the next one. They climb like a ladder until the king reaches the edge.
mates.rooks.ex1: Checkmate in one move. One rook cuts off the g-file, the other delivers mate.
mates.rooks.ex2: Checkmate in one move. One rook cuts off the seventh rank: with the other, mate on the eighth.
mates.rooks.ex3: Checkmate in two moves. First cut off the seventh rank with one rook, then give check on the eighth with the other.
mates.rooks.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. The black king is in the middle of the edge: cut off the seventh rank and he can only go one way.
mates.patterns.title: Famous mates
mates.patterns.intro: Some checkmates show up so often that they have a name. Learning to recognize them helps you find them in your games.
mates.patterns.ex1: Checkmate in one move. Anastasia's mate: the knight boxes in the king, the rook strikes along the file.
mates.patterns.ex2: Checkmate in one move. Arabian mate: rook and knight work together in the corner.
mates.patterns.ex3: Checkmate in one move. Boden's mate: two bishops cross their diagonals.
mates.patterns.ex4: Checkmate in one move. Damiano's mate: the pawn protects the queen.
mates.two.title: Mate in two
mates.two.intro: Sometimes checkmate comes in two moves: the first forces your opponent into a single reply, the second closes in on the king.
mates.two.ex1: Checkmate in two moves. Sacrifice a rook on the eighth rank.
mates.two.ex2: Checkmate in two moves. Sacrifice the queen to lure the king, then the rook shuts the back rank.
mates.two.ex3: Checkmate in two moves. Sacrifice the queen on h7: Anastasia's mate follows.
mates.two.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. Sacrifice the queen: the black king will be smothered by his own pieces.
mates.patterns-2.title: More famous mates
mates.patterns-2.intro: Here are more mates with a name. Look closely at the black pieces next to the king: they're often the ones blocking his way.
mates.patterns-2.ex1: Checkmate in one move. Epaulette mate: the black rooks stand on either side of the king like two epaulettes.
mates.patterns-2.ex2: Checkmate in one move. Greco's mate: the bishop controls g8 and the rook arrives on the h-file.
mates.patterns-2.ex3: Checkmate in one move. Cozio's mate: the queen gives check on the diagonal, protected by the pawn. The two escape squares the queen doesn't control are occupied by the black rook and pawn.
mates.patterns-2.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. Challenge: the Opera mate. Sacrifice the queen to remove the knight that defends d8, then rook and bishop deliver mate.
mates.guardian.title: The guardian
tactics.title: Tactics
tactics.hanging.title: Undefended pieces
tactics.hanging.intro: A piece is undefended if no other piece protects it. Before capturing, check whether the piece is defended: if it is, you might lose your own.
tactics.hanging.ex1: The queen can capture two pieces, but one is defended by the pawn. Take the undefended one.
tactics.hanging.ex2: The bishop attacks two black pieces. Capture the one nobody defends.
tactics.hanging.ex3: A black piece is undefended on the far side of the board. Find it and capture it.
tactics.hanging.ex4: The black knight is defended by the pawn. Capture it with the piece worth the least.
tactics.fork.title: The fork
tactics.fork.intro: A fork is an attack on two pieces at the same time. Your opponent can save only one, and you capture the other.
tactics.fork.ex1: Attack king and rook together with the knight, then capture the rook.
tactics.fork.ex2: A pawn can attack two pieces. Win a knight.
tactics.fork.ex3: Royal fork: attack king and queen together with the knight, then capture the queen.
tactics.fork.ex4: The queen can fork too: give check and attack the rook at the same time.
tactics.pin.title: The pin
tactics.pin.intro: A piece is pinned when it can't move because behind it stands the king, or a more valuable piece. A pinned piece is a target: attack it!
tactics.pin.ex1: The black knight is pinned to the king by the bishop. Attack it with a pawn.
tactics.pin.ex2: Pin the queen to the king with the rook: she can't leave the file anymore, and you win the queen for the rook.
tactics.pin.ex3: The pawn on d7 is pinned by the bishop and can't defend the knight. Capture it with the rook.
tactics.pin.ex4: Pin the rook to the king with the bishop: the rook won't be able to escape.
tactics.skewer.title: The skewer
tactics.skewer.intro: A skewer attacks a valuable piece that shields another one: when the first moves away, you capture the one behind it.
tactics.skewer.ex1: Give check to the king: when he moves, capture the queen behind him.
tactics.skewer.ex2: Skewer with the bishop: check the king, then capture the rook.
tactics.skewer.ex3: Skewer with the queen: check the king, then capture the rook.
tactics.skewer.ex4: Challenge: among all the checks, find the one that skewers, then capture the queen.
tactics.discovered.title: The discovered attack
tactics.discovered.intro: If you move a piece standing in front of a rook, bishop or queen, you uncover their attack. That way you attack with two pieces in a single move.
tactics.discovered.ex1: Move the knight: the rook gives check and the knight attacks the queen. Then capture her.
tactics.discovered.ex2: Move the knight with check: the uncovered bishop attacks the rook. Then capture it.
tactics.discovered.ex3: The bishop stands in front of the rook. Move it with check: the uncovered rook attacks the queen. Then capture her.
tactics.discovered.ex4: Move the bishop and the rook gives a discovered check. Take advantage of it to capture the strongest piece.
tactics.double-check.title: Double check
tactics.double-check.intro: In a double check two pieces give check at once. You can't block or capture both: the king has to move.
tactics.double-check.ex1: Checkmate in one move. The knight gives check and uncovers the rook: double check!
tactics.double-check.ex2: Checkmate in one move. Move the bishop: it gives check, and so does the rook.
tactics.double-check.ex3: Double check by knight and rook: the king must move. Then the knight captures the queen.
tactics.double-check.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. With the double check the king is forced to move. Then close in on him.
tactics.defender.title: Remove the defender
tactics.defender.intro: If an enemy piece is defended by just one piece, capture the defender: then the piece is left undefended and you take it.
tactics.defender.ex1: The black knight defends the bishop. Capture the knight, then take the bishop with the rook.
tactics.defender.ex2: The knight on c6 defends the other knight. Capture it with the bishop, then take the knight on e5 with the rook.
tactics.defender.ex3: The black bishop is defended only by the knight. Remove the defender, then capture the bishop.
tactics.defender.ex4: Challenge: the pawn on e6 defends two pieces, but it can't defend both. Capture the more valuable one.
tactics.overload.title: The overloaded piece
tactics.overload.intro: A piece is overloaded when it has two jobs: defending two pieces, or a piece and an important square. It can't do everything: attack one of the two and the other is left undefended.
tactics.overload.ex1: The black rook defends the knight and also the back rank. Capture the knight: if the rook recaptures, your rook delivers mate.
tactics.overload.ex2: The black queen defends the rook and also the e8 square. Capture the rook: if the queen recaptures, you deliver mate.
tactics.overload.ex3: The knight on f6 defends the knight on d5 and also the h7 square. Capture on d5: if it recaptures, the queen mates on h7.
tactics.overload.ex4: Challenge: the black queen defends both the bishop and the knight. Capture the bishop with the pawn: if the queen recaptures, the knight on c5 is left undefended.
tactics.decoy.title: The decoy
tactics.decoy.intro: To decoy means to lure an enemy piece, usually the king, onto a bad square. Often you sacrifice a piece: your opponent captures it and ends up exactly where you want.
tactics.decoy.ex1: Sacrifice the rook on h8: the king has to capture it. Then the knight attacks king and queen together.
tactics.decoy.ex2: Give check with the rook on d8: the black queen should capture it. Then the knight attacks king and queen together.
tactics.decoy.ex3: Capture on f7 with the bishop: the king has to recapture. Then the knight gives check and attacks the queen.
tactics.decoy.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. Challenge: sacrifice the rook on h7 to lure the king, then the queen delivers mate.
tactics.interference.title: Interference
tactics.interference.intro: A piece can defend from far away, along a line. If you put one of your pieces in the middle of that line, the defense is cut off.
tactics.interference.ex1: The black rook controls c8 along the eighth rank. Put your rook in between, on d8: if the black rook captures it, the pawn recaptures and becomes a queen.
tactics.interference.ex2: The black rook defends the bishop along the fifth rank. Put the knight in between with check: you win material, either the bishop or the rook in exchange for the knight.
tactics.interference.ex3: The rook on d8 defends the bishop on d4. Put the knight in between with check, protected by the pawn: you win either the bishop or the rook in exchange for the knight.
tactics.interference.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. Challenge: the black rook on h8 defends c8. Step in between with check: the pawn will do the rest.
tactics.zwischenzug.title: The in-between move
tactics.zwischenzug.intro: When your opponent captures, recapturing right away isn't always best. First look for a stronger move, like a check or a capture: then recapture.
tactics.zwischenzug.ex1: Black has taken your queen on e2. First capture the rook with check, then recapture the queen.
tactics.zwischenzug.ex2: Black has taken your queen on d1. First capture the rook with the knight, giving check, then recapture the queen.
tactics.zwischenzug.ex3: Black has taken your queen on b1. First promote the pawn with check, then recapture.
tactics.zwischenzug.ex4: Challenge: Black has taken your bishop on e2. Don't recapture right away: there's a check that wins more.
tactics.trapped.title: The trapped piece
tactics.trapped.intro: A piece is trapped when it has no safe squares to run to. Attack it: wherever it goes, you capture it.
tactics.trapped.ex1: The black bishop has taken a pawn on a2. Cut off its way out with a pawn: it won't be able to escape.
tactics.trapped.ex2: The black bishop on h5 is shut in by its own pawn on g6. Attack it with a pawn: it has nowhere to run.
tactics.trapped.ex3: The black knight is on the edge. Attack it with a pawn: every square it can go to is controlled.
tactics.trapped.ex4: Challenge: attack the bishop with a pawn. If it retreats to g6, the other pawn traps it.
tactics.xray.title: Battery and x-ray
tactics.xray.intro: Two pieces on the same line, one behind the other, form a battery. The rear piece backs up the front one as if by x-ray, and together they attack a square twice.
tactics.xray.ex1: Checkmate in one move. Queen and bishop form a battery on the diagonal: the bishop behind protects the queen.
tactics.xray.ex2: Checkmate in one move. The rook behind the queen protects her on the g-file.
tactics.xray.ex3: The black knight is attacked by two rooks and defended by only one. Capture it.
tactics.xray.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. Challenge: the rook on e1 protects the queen. Sacrifice the queen on e8, then the rook delivers mate.
tactics.guardian.title: The guardian
endgames.title: Endgames
endgames.queen.title: Queen checkmate
endgames.queen.intro: With king and queen against a lone king you always win: push the enemy king to the edge and close in with the help of your own king.
endgames.queen.ex1: Checkmate in one move. The white king protects the queen.
endgames.queen.ex2: Checkmate in one move. The black king is in the corner.
endgames.queen.ex3: Checkmate in two moves. Bring the king closer: then the queen delivers mate.
endgames.queen.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. First a quiet queen move: the black king is left with a single square.
endgames.rook.title: Rook checkmate
endgames.rook.intro: King and rook also beat a lone king. Your king stands face to face with the enemy king and the rook delivers mate on the edge.
endgames.rook.ex1: Checkmate in one move. The white king takes away the escape squares.
endgames.rook.ex2: Checkmate in one move. The kings face each other.
endgames.rook.ex3: Checkmate in two moves. Put your king face to face with the black one, then deliver mate with the rook.
endgames.rook.ex4: Checkmate in two moves. First bring the rook to g1: it cuts the black king off from the g-file and forces him to face your king.
endgames.square.title: The rule of the square
endgames.square.intro: A pawn runs to promote: the king can stop it only if he can step into its square, the square that runs from the pawn to the last rank.
endgames.square.ex1: The black pawn runs toward the first rank. Step into its square with the king to stop it.
endgames.square.ex2: The black king is outside your pawn's square: push the pawn and he can't catch it.
endgames.square.ex3: The black pawn runs toward the first rank. The king can enter the square from just one square: find it.
endgames.square.ex4: On its first move the pawn can take two steps: use them to get out of the black king's square.
endgames.opposition.title: Opposition
endgames.opposition.intro: When the two kings face each other with one square between them, the player to move has to give way. Having the opposition helps your king escort the pawn.
endgames.opposition.ex1: Your king is in front of the pawn. Step to the side, staying close: the pawn advances protected and goes on to promote.
endgames.opposition.ex2: The kings face each other. Find a winning move: step the king to the side or use the pawn's spare move.
endgames.opposition.ex3: Put your king face to face with the black one, with one square in between: that's the opposition.
endgames.opposition.ex4: Challenge: if you push the pawn right away it's a draw. Take the opposition with the king.
endgames.key-squares.title: Key squares
endgames.key-squares.intro: Every pawn has three key squares: if your king reaches them, the pawn promotes whoever is to move. If the pawn hasn't passed the middle of the board yet, they are the three squares two ranks ahead of it.
endgames.key-squares.ex1: The key squares of the e4 pawn are d6, e6 and f6. Take the king to one of them.
endgames.key-squares.ex2: The key squares of the d3 pawn are c5, d5 and e5. The black king guards two of them: go to the third.
endgames.key-squares.ex3: The pawn on e2 has its key squares too: d4, e4 and f4. Reach one of them before the black king.
endgames.key-squares.ex4: Challenge: the black king is close to your pawn and already stands on a key square. Take the one that's left free.
endgames.triangulation.title: Triangulation
endgames.triangulation.intro: Sometimes you wish it were your opponent's turn: his king would have to give way. Your king can lose a tempo by moving around three nearby squares, in a triangle, while the black king has only two good squares.
endgames.triangulation.ex1: Take the king to d2: when it's Black's turn, his king has to leave c4 and yours steps in.
endgames.triangulation.ex2: The black king on b4 is on the right square and you wish it were his turn. Start the triangle with your king: a single move wins.
endgames.triangulation.ex3: Your king is on d2, but it's your move. Lose a tempo with a step to the side: the black king will have to leave c4.
endgames.triangulation.ex4: Challenge: the same trick on the other side of the board. Find the king move that loses a tempo.
endgames.breakthrough.title: The breakthrough
endgames.breakthrough.intro: Sometimes three pawns against three can create a passed pawn by sacrificing: one advances, the others open the way.
endgames.breakthrough.ex1: Two pawns against one: sacrifice one and the other goes on to promote.
endgames.breakthrough.ex2: One black pawn holds back two. Sacrifice one to let the other through.
endgames.breakthrough.ex3: Break through with the pawns: sacrifice the central pawn, then another, until one reaches promotion.
endgames.breakthrough.ex4: Challenge: the same trick on the other wing. You find the right order of the pushes.
endgames.rook-behind.title: The rook behind the pawn
endgames.rook-behind.intro: The rook belongs behind passed pawns: behind your own it pushes it forward, behind the enemy's it holds it back. The further the pawn advances, the stronger the rook behind it becomes.
endgames.rook-behind.ex1: The black rook attacks your passed pawn. Defend it by putting the rook behind it.
endgames.rook-behind.ex2: Bring the rook behind the a5 pawn: get there along the rank.
endgames.rook-behind.ex3: The black pawn on b3 runs toward promotion. Stop it with the rook placed behind it.
endgames.rook-behind.ex4: Challenge: the black rook attacks f2. Don't defend it: put the rook behind your passed pawn, which is worth more.
endgames.wrong-bishop.title: The wrong bishop
endgames.wrong-bishop.intro: With a rook pawn, if the bishop can't go to the square where the pawn promotes, the defending king shuts himself in the corner and it's a draw. The defender runs to the corner, the attacker tries to stop him.
endgames.wrong-bishop.ex1: The black bishop only goes on dark squares, but h1 is light. Put the king in the corner: nobody can drive you out.
endgames.wrong-bishop.ex2: Now the wrong bishop is yours: h8 is dark. The black king runs toward the corner: block his way with the bishop.
endgames.wrong-bishop.ex3: The black king wants to reach h8. With the bishop, control the light squares he has to cross.
endgames.wrong-bishop.ex4: Challenge: the bishop checks you and the g4 pawn attacks the rook. Ke3 or Kf2 block the check but lose. Step out with the king to g2, next to the rook: if Black takes it, he is left with the wrong bishop.
endgames.guardian.title: The guardian
strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.value.title: Value changes
strategy.value.intro: Pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9: they are a guide, not a law. A pawn close to promotion is worth much more. And when you have more material, trade pieces: the advantage weighs more.
strategy.value.ex1: You are a knight up. Trade queens: without the queen Black has fewer tricks.
strategy.value.ex2: You are a knight up and Black is only a pawn up. Trade rooks to simplify the game.
strategy.value.ex3: The a2 pawn is about to become a queen: now it is worth more than your knight. Give up the knight to stop it.
strategy.value.ex4: Challenge: you are a pawn up. Trade rooks: the pawn endgame is won.
strategy.open-file.title: Rooks on open files
strategy.open-file.intro: A file is open when it has no pawns. There the rook runs all the way and often enters the seventh rank, where it attacks the enemy pawns.
strategy.open-file.ex1: The d-file is open. Put a rook on it before Black does.
strategy.open-file.ex2: One rook is already on the open file. Put the other one there too: two rooks together are even stronger.
strategy.open-file.ex3: From the open file, enter the seventh rank: there the rook attacks the black pawns.
strategy.open-file.ex4: Challenge: enter the seventh rank right away with one rook, then bring the other onto the open file, behind the first.
strategy.outpost.title: The knight's outpost
strategy.outpost.intro: An outpost is a square protected by one of your pawns that no enemy pawn can attack anymore. A knight there can't be driven away and controls everything around it.
strategy.outpost.ex1: The d5 square is protected by your pawns and no black pawn can attack it. Put your knight there.
strategy.outpost.ex2: The knight is far from the d5 outpost. Bring it there in two moves.
strategy.outpost.ex3: The black knight on f6 controls d5. Trade it off with the bishop, then put your knight on the outpost.
strategy.outpost.ex4: Challenge: Black no longer has the c and d pawns. Find the outpost for the knight: the e5 pawn helps you.
strategy.bishops.title: Good bishop and bad bishop
strategy.bishops.intro: A bishop is bad when your pawns stand on squares of its color and block its way; it is good when the pawns are on the other color. A bad bishop should be brought out from behind the pawns or traded.
strategy.bishops.ex1: Your pawns are on dark squares, like your bishop: it is bad. Get it out from c1 before it is shut in.
strategy.bishops.ex2: Your bishop is bad, the black one on d6 is good. Trade them.
strategy.bishops.ex3: Your bishop is good: the black pawns are stuck on light squares. Attack an undefended pawn with the bishop.
strategy.bishops.ex4: Challenge: the black bishop is bad and doesn't defend the dark squares. March the king in toward the black pawns.
strategy.passed-pawn.title: The passed pawn
strategy.passed-pawn.intro: A pawn is passed when no enemy pawn can stop it or capture it. Your passed pawns should be pushed; your opponent's should be blockaded, ideally with a knight right in front.
strategy.passed-pawn.ex1: You have two connected passed pawns. Push one: together they race toward promotion.
strategy.passed-pawn.ex2: On the queenside you have two pawns against one. Push the right one: after the trades you are left with a passed pawn.
strategy.passed-pawn.ex3: The black pawn on d4 is passed. Block it: put the knight right in front of it.
strategy.passed-pawn.ex4: Challenge: your a-pawn is passed and far from the black king. Push it: while the black king chases it, your king goes to pick up the black pawns.
strategy.active.title: Active pieces
strategy.active.intro: A piece is active when it has plenty of squares and attacks; on the edge or hemmed in by pawns it is passive. Improve your worst piece. In the endgame the king becomes an active piece too.
strategy.active.ex1: The knight on the edge controls few squares. Bring it closer to the center.
strategy.active.ex2: In the endgame the king is a strong piece. Bring him closer to the center.
strategy.active.ex3: The black rook has entered the second rank. Don't sit and defend: bring your rook to the seventh too, against the black pawns.
strategy.active.ex4: Challenge: find your worst piece and bring it into the game with the best move.
strategy.guardian.title: The guardian
openings.title: Openings
openings.center.title: The center
openings.center.intro: The four central squares (e4, d4, e5, d5) are the most important: from there the pieces control the whole board. Start with a central pawn.
openings.center.ex1: Take the center with a pawn.
openings.center.ex2: Black hasn't taken the center. Bring your other pawn to the center too.
openings.center.ex3: The black pawn on d5 attacks your pawn on e4. Capture it.
openings.center.ex4: Push the other central pawn: that way you attack the black pawn on e5.
openings.develop.title: Develop your pieces
openings.develop.intro: To develop means to bring knights and bishops into play in the first moves, before moving the same pieces again or the queen.
openings.develop.ex1: Bring a knight or a bishop into play.
openings.develop.ex2: Play the Italian Game: knight to f3, then bishop to c4.
openings.develop.ex3: The black knight attacks the pawn on e4. Defend it by developing a knight.
openings.develop.ex4: The black queen came out early. Develop a piece that attacks her without getting captured.
openings.castle.title: Castling
openings.castle.intro: In the first moves, castle early: the king goes to safety behind the pawns and the rook comes into play.
openings.castle.ex1: Put your king to safety with kingside castling.
openings.castle.ex2: Now castle queenside: the king heads toward the a1 rook.
openings.castle.ex3: To castle kingside, the squares between king and rook must be empty. Move the bishop, then castle.
openings.castle.ex4: Challenge: knight to f3, then bishop out, then castle kingside.
openings.scholar.title: Scholar's mate
openings.scholar.intro: Scholar's mate hits the f7 square, defended only by the king, with queen and bishop. Knowing how to deliver it is useful, but knowing how to stop it is even more useful.
openings.scholar.ex1: Checkmate in one move. Black forgot to defend f7.
openings.scholar.ex2: Checkmate in one move. This time the queen is on f3.
openings.scholar.ex3: Now Black threatens mate on f2 with queen and bishop. Defend f2 with the queen, or block the diagonal with a pawn.
openings.scholar.ex4: Black still threatens mate on f2 with queen and bishop. Stop the threat by developing a knight.
openings.guardian.title: The guardian
capablanca.title: Capablanca's school
capablanca.race.title: Who promotes first
capablanca.race.intro: Capablanca teaches you to count. When two pawns race to promote, count each one's moves: whoever arrives first wins, and it's even better if the new queen controls the square where the other pawn promotes.
capablanca.race.ex1: Count the moves: your pawn arrives before the black one, and from a8 the queen controls h1. Push!
capablanca.race.ex2: Capablanca's position: no king can stop the pawns, so count. Push the a-pawn two steps: the pawn on b5 will help you break through later.
capablanca.race.ex3: Black is racing with the h-pawn. Don't waste time with the king: every move counts, keep pushing.
capablanca.race.ex4: Challenge: break through with the b-pawn. Then don't recapture on b6: push the a-pawn, so your queen is born on a8 and controls h1, where Black promotes.
capablanca.distant-opposition.title: Distant opposition
capablanca.distant-opposition.intro: The opposition works from far away too. If the kings are on the same file and there's an odd number of squares between them, the player who has just moved has the opposition; if the number is even, it's the player to move. Capablanca used it both to attack and to defend.
capablanca.distant-opposition.ex1: Capablanca's position: there are six squares between the kings, an even number, and it's your move. Advance straight toward the black king.
capablanca.distant-opposition.ex2: If you run toward b5 it's a draw: count the moves. Stay in front of the black king and don't let him through toward h4.
capablanca.distant-opposition.ex3: Black made a waiting move with the king. Don't go straight in front of him, but take back the distant opposition: find the king move.
capablanca.distant-opposition.ex4: Challenge: you are a pawn down, but the distant opposition saves you. King to f1 looks natural and loses: find the right square for the king.
capablanca.combinations.title: Capablanca's combinations
capablanca.combinations.intro: Often the real threat is hidden behind a sacrifice. Capablanca shows how pieces working together against a weak point near the king deliver mate or win material. Before you move, look at all the checks.
capablanca.combinations.ex1: Sacrifice the knight on f6 with check: the g-file opens. Then queen check and the bishop on b2 delivers mate.
capablanca.combinations.ex2: Capablanca's position: Black put the rook on e8 to attack on e1, but the strongest threat is yours. Sacrifice the queen on h7, then the rook drops onto the h-file: the bishop on b2 protects it.
capablanca.combinations.ex3: Capablanca's position: the knight on d7 defends f6. Remove it with the bishop: if the queen recaptures, knight to f6 with check wins.
capablanca.combinations.ex4: Challenge, Capablanca's position: you are a piece down. Take the knight on c6, check on e7 and trade pieces. In the end bring the queen to the attack: from d7 she hits both bishops at once.
capablanca.opening-rules.title: The rules of the opening
capablanca.opening-rules.intro: Capablanca's advice: bring your pieces out quickly, knights first and then bishops, and don't move the same piece twice unless it wins material. Whoever forgets this falls into traps.
capablanca.opening-rules.ex1: Black moved the bishop before the knights and traded it. With the queen, attack b7 and f7 together.
capablanca.opening-rules.ex2: Black recaptured on e5 with the knight instead of the pawn. Capture the knight, even though your queen stays under attack.
capablanca.opening-rules.ex3: Checkmate in two moves. Black took the queen: now bishop and knights deliver mate.
capablanca.opening-rules.ex4: Challenge: Black developed the bishop before a knight. Sacrifice the bishop on f7, give check with the knight and take the bishop on g4.
capablanca.guardian.title: The guardian
